aggregate.doc:
Incrementally maintained monoid fold: `lift` maps an element into
the aggregate domain, `combine` merges two aggregates, `identity`
is the unit. O(log n) per change; see the Rust docs for the
associativity contract.
Not-ready elements are left out and counted as for `reduce`, and
`lift` and `combine` never see a not-ready or `Incomplete` value.

count.doc:
The number of ready elements, `Incomplete` with the number of
not-ready and `Incomplete` elements when there are any.

reduce.doc:
`fold_fn` of the list of rows, with not-ready elements left out
and an `Incomplete` element's `value` in; `Incomplete` when any
element is, counting each not-ready element once and each
`Incomplete` element's `missing`.

incr.Incomplete.doc:
`value` computed with `missing` contributions left out because they
were not ready. Through queries `missing` counts contributions: a query
reading two totals that both miss one element reports 2. A collection
total counts distinct elements.

__new__.doc: Create and return a new object.  See help(type) for accurate signature.

incr.KeyedCollection.doc:
Rows by key: a collection of `(key, row)` pairs holding at most one row
per key, with keys matched as a dict matches them. `collection` is the
rows as a `Collection`, for the operators.

Rows must be hashable. A change hashes each added pair's row in the pair
collection, and each added or removed row again in `collection`'s output
staging, which also runs one row `__eq__` per removed row; before Python
3.14, which caches a tuple's hash, a removed pair's row is hashed in the
pair collection too. So an upsert that inserts pays two row `__hash__`
calls, one that replaces pays three (four before 3.14) and two row
`__eq__` against the held row, and one with an `==` row changes nothing.

Key and row methods run as value code: one that calls into incr during
an operation on the collection raises `RuntimeError`, which the
operation raises, changing nothing.

`label` names the collection's group in `Runtime.graph_summary`: it
labels the pair and row collections' version nodes, and the group
reports the key count as `"keys"`.

__new__.doc: Create and return a new object.  See help(type) for accurate signature.

get.doc:
The row held for `key`, or `None`. Registers no dependency: inside a
query, read a key with `ctx.get_key(kc, key)` so the query reruns
when that key's row changes.

items.doc:
A new list of the held `(key, row)` tuples, in no particular order.
Registers no dependency, like `get`.

keys.doc:
A new list of the held keys, in no particular order. Registers no
dependency, like `get`.

reconcile.doc:
Make the held rows equal `rows`, a mapping or an iterable of
`(key, row)` pairs (a later pair for a key wins), in one atomic
change. Returns how many keys were `(inserted, replaced, removed)`.

remove.doc: Remove `key`'s pair. Raises `KeyError` if no row is held for it.

upsert.doc:
Hold `row` for `key`: nothing happens if the held row is `==` to
it, otherwise the pair is replaced or inserted.

__new__.doc: Create and return a new object.  See help(type) for accurate signature.

incr.NotReady.doc: The base of every value standing for a result that is not ready.

incr.Overlay.doc:
`with rt.overlay() as ov:` runs candidate changes against the live
graph and puts the base graph back exactly on exit, also when the body
raises. Mutations journal their inverse; operations that cannot be
undone raise inside the block. Inverses re-run user `Hash` and `Eq`, so
those must be deterministic and must not raise; if one does, the
runtime is poisoned and only `close` still works. A restored collection
may hold its elements in another order, so `aggregate` combines must be
associative and commutative, `sort_by_key` output is exact up to the
order among equal keys, and `group_by` keeps a group a candidate
emptied or created.

incr.Pending.doc: A result still being fetched, for `key` when it came from a lookup.

__new__.doc: Create and return a new object.  See help(type) for accurate signature.
Create and return a new object.  See help(type) for accurate signature.

close.doc:
Drop the engine and everything it holds: values, closures and the
Python objects they capture. Every later call on this runtime or an
object derived from it raises. Refused while a call on it is running,
and for the runtime of a store, which `store.close()` closes.

compute_stats.doc:
`{group: {"recomputed", "cutoff", "verified", "elapsed_ns"}}`
counted since stats were enabled or last reset, grouped by the
label up to its first `/` (`None` for unlabelled nodes).
`recomputed` counts every run that landed, `cutoff` those whose
value was equal, and `elapsed_ns` closure time net of nested
computes. `reset=True` zeroes the counts after reading them.

create_lookup.doc:
The lookup node for `key`: an input created as `Pending(key)`, and
queued for `drain_pending_lookups`, the first time `key` is asked
for here or through `RuntimeRef.lookup`. No query owns it, so it
keeps its value when the queries reading it stop.

create_query.doc:
A query computing `py_func(runtime_ref)`. `fallback(ids)` or a
`Fixpoint` resolves a cycle through it; `replay=True` lets a read
past the frame budget replay instead of nesting.

delete_node.doc:
Delete a node and recycle its slot. Every surviving handle to it
raises on use. The node must have no dependents.

delete_with_dependents.doc:
Delete the node, every node that depends on it (transitively)
and every node an operator created for them. Returns how many
nodes were deleted; 0 if the node was already gone. A query that
has never run is not reached, and raises as stale on first use.

drain_dirtied_watched.doc:
The watched nodes a change moved off Clean since the last drain,
each once, in the order the changes reached them. A node deleted
since is left out.

drain_pending_lookups.doc:
The keys queued since the last drain whose lookup is still
`Pending`, each once.

enable_compute_stats.doc:
Starts or stops compute stats, which count per node the runs that
landed a value, those cut off, the verifications that found it
clean and its closure time. Off by default.

get.doc:
The node's value: a `NotReady` value as stored, and an `Incomplete`
value's `value`.

get_key.doc:
The row `kc` holds for `key`, or `None`, as stored. Outside a query
it creates nothing; `ctx.get_key` is the read that depends on the
key. Raises `ValueError` for a keyed collection of another runtime.

get_with_status.doc:
`(value, status)`: the value `get` returns, and `None`, the
`NotReady` value, or the `Incomplete` value.

graph_snapshot.doc:
The graph as a list of `{"id", "kind", "label", "dependencies",
"dependents"}` dicts. With any argument given, a breadth-first walk
from `roots` (node handles or collections) returns
`{"nodes": [...], "truncated": bool}` instead: `direction` is
`"dependencies"` (default), `"dependents"` or `"both"`; `depth`
counts edges from a root; `label_prefix` filters the returned nodes
while the walk still passes through the others; `limit` caps them.
Each returned node keeps its full dependency and dependent lists.

graph_summary.doc:
`{"groups": [{"label", "kind", "nodes"}], "edges": [{"from", "to",
"count"}]}` over the live graph, grouped by the label up to its
first `/` (`None` for unlabelled nodes); `kind` is "input",
"compute" or "mixed". An edge inside one group has `from == to`.
A group a labelled `KeyedCollection` names also has `"keys"`, the
collection's key count (summed over such collections). Walks every
node under the engine's read lock, so the cost is linear in the
node count.

is_alive.doc:
True while the node exists in this runtime. False after it is
deleted, and for a node from another runtime.

memory_stats.doc:
Memory held by this runtime: `{"bytes", "nodes", "py_refs",
"by_kind", "by_label"}`. `bytes` estimates what the engine holds from
sizes and capacities (node slots, values' own slots, closures' captures,
dependency lists, labels, collection logs and operator state); the
Python objects themselves are not in it. `py_refs` counts the
references the engine holds to Python objects: node values,
collection elements and logged changes, operator state, keyed
indexes, and every callable handed to it, but not the engine's own
copies of a `window`'s windows. `by_kind` splits nodes into "input",
"query" and "collection" (a collection's version node), and puts all
collection and operator state under "collection". `by_label` totals
labelled nodes by the label up to its first `/`, with a collection's
state under the label of its `version_node`; callables are not
attributed to labels. Walks the whole graph; nothing is counted
between calls.

observe.doc:
Register `callback` to fire on `stabilize()` whenever the node's
value changed since the last firing.

overlay.doc:
Run candidate changes against the live graph and put it back
exactly on exit; see `Overlay`.

resolve_lookups.doc:
Set each lookup to its value, from a mapping or an iterable of
`(key, value)` pairs, creating the ones not asked for yet. Not
atomic: if a key's `__hash__` or `__eq__` raises, the keys before it
are set.

retry_lookups.doc: Set each key's lookup back to `Pending(key)` and queue it again.

set_max_frames.doc: The frame budget past which a replayable query's read replays.

set_max_stack_bytes.doc: A stack budget in bytes beside the frame budget; 0 turns it off.

set_placeholder.doc:
The value a replayed read returns in place of the node it wanted.
Set once per runtime.

stabilize.doc:
Bring observed nodes up to date and fire callbacks for changed
values.

try_delete_node.doc:
Delete the node and the nodes it owns only if none of them has a
dependent. Raises `HasDependentsError` (deleting nothing) if one
does, and `KeyError` if the node is not alive.

try_get.doc:
Like `get`, but a cycle that leaves the node without a value raises
`CycleError` as an ordinary exception.

unwatch.doc: Stop reporting the node, and drop its pending report.

watch.doc:
Report the node through `drain_dirtied_watched()` whenever a change
moves it off Clean. A node that has no current value when watched
is reported at once.

incr.RuntimeRef.doc:
Read-only runtime handle passed to query closures. The pointer is
nulled out after the callback returns to make stale captures fail
loudly rather than silently corrupt memory.

child_input.doc:
The input child named `key` of this query, created with `init()`
the first time this query asks for it. Children this query stops
asking for are deleted when it next lands.

child_query.doc:
The query child named `key`, created with `f` the first time, like
`child_input`; the options apply only when the call creates it.

get.doc:
The node's value. A `NotReady` value makes this query's value that
value; an `Incomplete` one gives its `value` and makes this query's
value `Incomplete`, with every `missing` it read added up.

get_key.doc:
The row `kc` holds for `key`, or `None`, read as `get` reads a node,
with a dependency on that key alone: the query reruns when a write
changes this key's row, inserts it or removes it, and not for other
keys. Raises `ValueError` for a keyed collection of another runtime.

get_key_status.doc:
`(row, status)` for `kc`'s `key` as `get_status` gives them, read
with the dependency of `get_key`; `(None, None)` for an absent key.

get_status.doc:
`(value, status)` as `Runtime.get_with_status` gives them, with
neither rule of `get` applied.

lookup.doc:
The value of `key`'s lookup (see `Runtime.create_lookup`), read as
`get` reads a node: `Pending` makes this query's value `Pending`.

memo.doc:
The value of `table`'s entry for `key` (see `Store.memo_table`),
restored from the memo or computed, read as `get` reads a node.

try_get.doc:
Like `get`, but a cycle that leaves the node without a value
raises `CycleError` as an ordinary exception the query may catch.

incr.Unavailable.doc:
A value withheld for `reason`. As a collection element, `row` is the
element it stands in for: keyed operators key on it, and `map` and
`filter` apply to it.

__new__.doc: Create and return a new object.  See help(type) for accurate signature.

incr.persist.Batch.doc:
The writes of a `with store.batch() as b:` block; see `Store.batch`.

In an `on_exit` batch keyed writes compose per key against the rows
each key held when first staged, so `b.upsert` twice on one key, or
`b.upsert` then `b.remove`, leave exactly the final pair, and
`b.remove` raises `KeyError` for a key neither held nor staged; the
collection takes the staged keys only once the append has landed. In
an `on_write` batch each write applies at once, and `b.remove` raises
`KeyError` for a key holding no row at that point.

retry.doc:
Appends the run of an `on_write` batch whose append raised, with
the same `append_at`, so it lands at most once, and returns the
position of its last record. Raises what the append raises, keeping
the run for another retry; `PersistError` once the run has landed;
`RuntimeError` for an `on_exit` batch, inside the block, or after a
block that raised.

incr.persist.Busy.doc: Another handle holds the memo checkpoint lock or has written a newer generation: the checkpoint wrote nothing and can be retried.

incr.persist.InvalidCompaction.doc: `compact(upto, ..)` was given an `upto` below the snapshot position or beyond the tail; constructed as `InvalidCompaction(upto, snapshot_at, tail)`.

incr.persist.Memo.doc:
An open memo: `memo.get_or_insert(table, key)` gives an entry's node, and
`memo.checkpoint()` writes the live entries to the backend.

checkpoint.doc:
Writes every live entry whose dependencies are persisted to the
backend as the next generation, and returns how many it `written`,
`merged` from the previous generation, `evicted` and so on. Raises
`Busy` when another handle is checkpointing. Raises `ValueError`
naming the table when an entry's key or value did not round-trip
through its codec: the generation was still written, without that
entry, which is recomputed on the next run.

get_or_insert.doc:
The node of `table`'s entry for `key`: the live one, or one restored
from the memo, or a new one. Read it with `runtime.get`. Inside an
overlay it computes fresh and records nothing, so no candidate value
is restored from the memo or reaches it.

incr.persist.MemoTable.doc:
A memo table of a store: pass it to `memo.get_or_insert` and
`ctx.memo`.

incr.persist.MemoryBackend.doc:
A log held in process memory: the reference implementation of the
backend protocol, for tests and development. Stores opened on the same
object share its log; `read_only()` gives a handle that cannot write.

__new__.doc: Create and return a new object.  See help(type) for accurate signature.

append_at.doc:
Appends `records` right after `after` if the log's tail is
still `after`, returning the last position; raises
`TailMoved`, writing nothing, when the tail is elsewhere.

incr.persist.MemoryMemo.doc:
A memo store held in process memory: the reference implementation of
the memo backend protocol, for tests and development. Stores opened on
the same object share its generations.

__new__.doc: Create and return a new object.  See help(type) for accurate signature.

incr.persist.PersistError.doc: A store or backend failure that no Python exception describes better.

incr.persist.ReadOnly.doc: A write reached a handle opened read-only.

incr.persist.Store.doc:
Persisted inputs and collections over a backend, and the runtime that
reads them.

`store.input(key, default, codec)` and `store.collection(key, codec)`
declare a key and return its node or `Collection`; `codec` is any object
with `encode(obj) -> bytes` and `decode(bytes) -> obj`. Two contracts
bind it: `decode(encode(x)) == x`, and `encode` is deterministic (equal
values give equal bytes), since fingerprints hash the bytes. A codec
need not know `Pending`, `LookupFailed`, `Unavailable` or `Incomplete`:
those persist as themselves, and only their `row`, `value`, `key` and
`reason` go through the codec. A value written to a slot with no codec
raises, naming the slot.

Persisted nodes are written through the store (`store.set`,
`store.insert`, ...); `runtime.set` and a persisted collection's own
`insert`, `delete`, `extend` and `replace` raise `RuntimeError`.

batch.doc:
Starts a batch of `b.set`, `b.insert`, `b.delete`, `b.replace`,
`b.upsert`, `b.remove` and `b.reconcile`, appended to the log as
one run, so a restore sees all of them or none.

`apply="on_exit"` (the default) collects the writes and appends and
applies them on leaving the block; a block that raises writes
nothing, and reads inside it see the values from before it.

`apply="on_write"` applies each write at once, so reads inside the
block see it, and appends the run on leaving the block with the
backend's `append_at`, right after the position the store had
applied; a backend without `append_at` refuses it with
`PersistError`. Entering catches up with the log and runs a due
`auto_checkpoint_records` checkpoint, so none falls between the
batch's records. Until the run lands every other store call that
writes, declares, refreshes or checkpoints, a memo checkpoint and a
second batch raise `PersistError`. If the append raises, the block
raises it and the batch keeps its run: `b.retry()` appends it again
and lands it at most once. A block that raises, or a batch dropped
before its run lands, poisons the store, since the runtime holds
writes the log never receives: every later store call raises
`PersistError` and the way out is to close the store and open the
log again. A backend that fences this writer keeps raising, so its
way out is the same.

checkpoint.doc:
Folds the log into a snapshot, compacting it, and returns the
position the snapshot covers.

close.doc: Closes the store and its runtime: every later call on either raises.

collection.doc:
Declares the collection `key`, which starts with its logged elements,
and returns it as a `Collection`. Write it with `store.insert`,
`store.delete`, `store.replace` and `store.extend`.

delete.doc:
Removes one occurrence of `row` from a persisted collection. Removing
an absent row is logged and changes nothing.

extend.doc: Appends every row of `rows` in one logged step.

input.doc:
Declares the input `key`, which starts at its logged value or else at
`default`, and returns its node. Write it with `store.set`.

insert.doc: Appends one occurrence of `row` to a persisted collection.

keyed_collection.doc:
Declares the keyed collection `key`: a `KeyedCollection` over a
persisted collection of `(key, row)` pairs, holding the pairs the
log restores. `key_codec` and `codec` encode the
keys and the rows, under the contracts of `store.input`. Write it
with `store.upsert`, `store.remove`, `store.reconcile` or a
`store.batch`; its own writes raise. `label` names the collection's
group in `graph_summary`, labelling its pair and row nodes.

memo_table.doc:
Declares the memo table `name`, whose entries `func(ctx, key)`
computes, and returns it. `ctx` is the `RuntimeRef` queries receive,
and `ctx.memo(table, key)` reads another entry as a dependency.
`key_codec` and `codec` encode the keys and the values under the
contracts of `store.input`, and `func` must be a pure function of
its key and what it reads through `ctx`. Bump `version` when it
changes meaning: entries are kept only while the name and version
match. Declare every table before `store.open_memo`.

open.doc:
Convert a function to be a static method.

A static method does not receive an implicit first argument.
To declare a static method, use this idiom:

     class C:
         @staticmethod
         def f(arg1, arg2, argN):
             ...

It can be called either on the class (e.g. C.f()) or on an instance
(e.g. C().f()). Both the class and the instance are ignored, and
neither is passed implicitly as the first argument to the method.

Static methods in Python are similar to those found in Java or C++.
For a more advanced concept, see the classmethod builtin.

open_memo.doc:
Opens the memo over `backend`, an object that implements the memo
backend protocol (see `incr.persist.MemoryMemo`), and loads its
current generation. Entries written under another `build_id`, or by
a table of another name, version or type, are ignored.

reconcile.doc:
Makes a persisted keyed collection hold exactly `rows`, as
`KeyedCollection.reconcile` does, in one logged step. Returns how
many keys were `(inserted, replaced, removed)`.

refresh.doc:
Applies the records other writers appended since this store last
read the log, across a compaction too, and returns the position it
has applied through.

remove.doc:
Removes `key`'s pair from a persisted keyed collection. Raises
`KeyError` if no row is held for it.

replace.doc:
Removes one occurrence of `old`, if present, and inserts `new`, as
one logged step.

runtime.doc:
The runtime that reads the store's nodes. Close the store, not the
runtime.

set.doc: Sets a persisted input: the value is logged, then applied.

stats.doc:
`position` (the last log position applied), `snapshot_position`
(the snapshot this store last wrote or crossed, 0 if none) and
`records_since_checkpoint`, read without touching the backend.

upsert.doc:
Holds `row` for `key` in a persisted keyed collection, as
`KeyedCollection.upsert` does, logging the change.

incr.persist.TailMoved.doc: A backend's `append_at(after, records)` found the log's tail somewhere other than `after` and wrote nothing. A Python backend raises it to say so.

incr.persist._conformance.doc:
Runs the cases of `kind` (`"store"` or `"memo"`), or only `case`.
Returns each case's name mapped to `None` on a pass or the panic
message.

incr.persist.conformance.ConformanceFail.doc: A backend failed a conformance case; `case` names it.

incr.persist.conformance.cases.doc: The names of the `kind` (`"log"` or `"memo"`) cases, in run order.

incr.persist.conformance.run_log_backend.doc:
Runs every log backend case against handles from `factory`, raising
`ConformanceFailure` naming the first case that fails.

incr.persist.conformance.run_memo_backen.doc:
Runs every memo backend case against handles from `factory`, raising
`ConformanceFailure` naming the first case that fails.
